mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate below 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings expectations for industrial firms and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening of monetary policy and rising inflation, increasing real interest rates and depressing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.7%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent monthly decline in both HOUST and RSAFS signals a drop in housing and retail sales activity, reducing consumer spending and corporate revenues, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both decline month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 35% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in PAYEMS above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports corporate earnings and justifies higher equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.7%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS is below 1% and CPIAUCSL is rising above 3% year-over-year, the real interest rate becomes negative, incentivizing risk-taking and supporting equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: low nominal rates with rising inflation
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.
